experiments.name: candidate_ranker_synthetic Heldout Generalization Benchmark
experiments.description: Non-generative candidate ranker (candidate_ranker_synthetic, 22 usable cases from 35-case synthetic training fixture, character granularity, conservative selection gates) evaluated on heldout_generalization fixture (63 cases) and saturated suite (234 cases). Training fixture (ctx-train-*) has disjoint IDs and zero expected-sentence overlap with all evaluation fixtures. The ranker matches baseline exactly at 39/63 on heldout (0 changed, 0 improved, 0 regressed) with p95 128us latency. On the saturated suite, the ranker scores 182/234 (+1 vs current evaluator baseline of 181/234) but regresses 52 cases vs deterministic 234/234. The heldout gate fails: the count-based ranker has zero non-baseline evidence on heldout because exact feature-vector overlap is insufficient.
experiments.conclusion: candidate_ranker_synthetic does not beat deterministic 41/63 on heldout_generalization. The count-feature approach cannot generalize to disjoint evaluation contexts because zero training examples share exact feature vectors with heldout cases. On the saturated suite, it shows a modest +1 over the current baseline but regresses 52 cases vs deterministic 234/234. The synthetic training fixture provides insufficient context overlap for the ranker's exact-string feature matching to fire on either evaluation set. Recommend exploring alternative approaches (embedding-based similarity, classifier over n-grams, or true tiny language model with constrained decoding) that can generalize beyond exact feature overlap.
gate_reasons: candidate_ranker exact matches 39 < deterministic 41 on heldout (RER -9.09%)
non_baseline_evidence_cases = 0 on heldout: ranker cannot override baseline without training context overlap
52 regressed cases on saturated suite vs deterministic 234/234
Count-based feature matching is inherently local and does not generalize to unseen contexts
verification: fixture audit: ctx-train-* IDs and 0 expected-sentence overlap with heldout/canonical eval fixtures
train with --exclude-fixture heldout_generalization --exclude-id-prefix hg- (usable=22, excluded=0 because synthetic training IDs are disjoint)
next_steps: Abandon count-based candidate-ranker-v1 approach for disjoint-evaluation scenarios because exact feature matching cannot generalize
For generalization beyond exact string overlap: evaluate embedding-based similarity (encode context + candidate) or a trained classifier over character/reading n-grams
Alternatively, accept that the deterministic reranker (41/63 heldout, 234/234 saturated) is the correct production path and invest in expanding context rules rather than learned rankers
Any future learned ranker must use training data with measurable context overlap to evaluation cases or use a feature representation that supports generalization
